rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline by testing a simple rna_only model with singleprofile and pca_n2000 encoder. This clarifies the baseline performance of RNA-only features and isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, providing critical initial data for subsequent comparisons.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It directly addresses whether multiprofile improves performance while using a simple aggregation method, reducing uncertainty about key design choices without overcomplicating the configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings (config_002) outperform singleprofile (config_001) with avgpool aggregation. This experiment tests the effect of replacing PCA with scvi_n200 RNA encoder while maintaining multiprofile and avgpool, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder. It balances exploration of key design choices (encoder) with exploitation of the promising multiprofile direction.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with multiprofile and scvi_n200 encoder achieve higher accuracy (0.65) than pca_n2000. This experiment tests if changing aggregation from avgpool (config_005) to transformer could further improve performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the promising RNA-only multiprofile direction with exploration of architectural improvements.

The existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 with transformer aggregation in multiprofile (config_006) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests combining this RNA encoder with image data (resnet50) using avgpool and concat fusion, isolating the effect of multimodal integration. It balances exploitation of the current best RNA model with exploration of multimodal potential, which could yield higher accuracy.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006, 0.652970 accuracy) outperform other RNA-only and multimodal configurations. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt while retaining transformer aggregation (a key factor in previous success) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, which remains uncertain despite scvi_n200's strong performance. This balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a new encoder, maximizing the chance of finding a better configuration within the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.652970). This experiment tests whether combining this strong RNA representation with image data (resnet50 encoder) and weighted fusion can further improve performance. It isolates the effect of multimodal fusion while reusing the top-performing RNA encoder and aggregation method, balancing exploitation of known strengths with exploration of multimodal potential.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l image encoder while keeping other components the same, to determine if a more advanced image encoder further improves performance. This isolates the effect of the image encoder choice, which is critical for multimodal models.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve the highest accuracy (config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and fusion settings to explore if the RNA encoder choice impacts performance. It clarifies whether scgpt (lower prior accuracy) could match scvi_n200's performance, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of RNA encoder alternatives.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using the same image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and fusion method (weighted) with a different RNA encoder (pca_n2000) and singleprofile setting can improve performance. It clarifies the impact of RNA encoder and profile setting on multimodal performance, prioritizing exploration of key design choices.
